title: White Gem F1 Corn (White Gem): Characteristics
metaDescription: White Gem F1 corn is a glutinous hybrid corn variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: White Gem F1 corn is a glutinous hybrid corn variety, also sold or known as White Gem or White Gem waxy corn. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical Corporation (Condor Quality Seeds brand).

heroImage.alt: A cornfield on a hillside in Pilar, Capiz, its leaves drying close to harvest, the kind of farm where White Gem F1 corn is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for White Gem or White Gem waxy corn, this is the same corn. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [corn variety finder](/crop-varieties/corn), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Pagtatanim ng mais, step by step](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-mais).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: 65 to 70 days after sowing. Yield, by the seller's count: 10 to 15 t/ha of husked ears (company figure). No trial on record checks these figures yet, so treat them as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit corn fields most often: [Asian corn borer](/pests/asian-corn-borer), [banded leaf and sheath blight](/diseases/banded-leaf-and-sheath-blight), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Corn ear rot](/diseases/corn-ear-rot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a new white waxy (malagkit) corn hybrid in Allied Botanical's line. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual corn on the same ground.
Where and when to plant White Gem F1 corn

Start with the color your buyer pays for: yellow corn goes to feed mills, while white and glutinous corn go to the table. Next, pick between a hybrid, which yields more but needs new seed every season, and an open pollinated variety, whose seed you can save. Then match the island group in its recommendation, because trials in Luzon and Mindanao give different winners. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for corn](/land-preparation/corn-land-preparation).

items.q: Is White Gem the same as White Gem F1?
items.a: Yes. White Gem is another name for White Gem F1. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of White Gem F1?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
